title: Special Episode: A Crash Course in Dembow, a Misunderstood Pantry Staple and Simple Tips to Keep Calm and Carry On

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·罗森，欢迎收听《重新构想者》，这是一个全方位探讨设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 回想当年我在黑胶唱片时代去夜店当DJ的时候，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 每天晚上你都要带300件你最珍爱的宝贝去上班，你把DJ台变成了一个充满美丽50年历史老物件的流动快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在，请在您喜爱的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重新构想者》。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Kim Severson, a food writer with The New York Times, back once again with more from our new series, NYT Shorts.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是《纽约时报》的美食专栏作家金·塞弗森，我们的全新栏目《纽约时报短片》又和大家见面了。

sentences.en: These are bite-sized dispatches from our reporters, editors, and critics.
sentences.zh: 这些都是来自我们记者、编辑和评论员的精彩短讯。

sentences.en: You'll be the first to know about their latest obsessions and what they see coming next.
sentences.zh: 你们将率先了解他们最新的痴迷以及他们所预见的未来趋势。

sentences.en: It's just an amazing thing to watch.
sentences.zh: 看着这一幕简直太棒了。

sentences.en: I love it.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢了。

sentences.en: I'm calling it now.
sentences.zh: 我现在就话先放这儿了。

sentences.en: I'm not afraid to call it now.
sentences.zh: 我可不怕现在就把话放这儿。

sentences.en: It's the movie that unlocked my love for cinema.
sentences.zh: 就是这部电影开启了我对电影的热爱。

sentences.en: I am crying.
sentences.zh: 我在哭。

sentences.en: I'm crying a little bit.
sentences.zh: 我有点想哭。

sentences.en: Find them and more on our new app, NYT Audio.
sentences.zh: 欢迎在我们的全新应用《纽约时报音频》中寻找这些及更多内容。

sentences.en: It's available now to all our subscribers.
sentences.zh: 所有订阅用户现已均可使用。

sentences.en: First up, Isabella Herrera writes about music for The Times.
sentences.zh: 首先，伊莎贝拉·埃雷拉为《时报》撰写音乐文章。

sentences.en: And today, she's giving us a crash course in Dembo.
sentences.zh: 今天，她将为我们上一堂关于登博乐（Dembow）的入门课。

sentences.en: When I was a kid, I would go on these trips to the Dominican Republic to visit my family.
sentences.zh: 小时候，我会随家人去多米尼加共和国旅行。

sentences.en: We would make sure we went to the beach at some point.
sentences.zh: 我们总会抽时间去一趟海滩。

sentences.en: It was about, you know, two hours away from Santiago, where my family is from.
sentences.zh: 从我老家圣地亚哥出发，开车大概要两个小时左右吧。

sentences.en: On the way to the beach, we would often see these vans that were, like, really just, you know, had huge speakers, like, just covered in subwoofers.
sentences.zh: 在去海滩的路上，我们经常会看到一些面包车，上面装满了巨大的音响，基本上全被低音炮覆盖了。

sentences.en: There would be a lot of gasolineras, which, you know, these gas stations where a lot of these vans would just kind of park.
sentences.zh: 路上会有很多加油站，你知道的，许多这种面包车就会停在这些加油站附近。

sentences.en: And it was basically, like, as soon as you pulled up, you could just feel the bass.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是，你的车刚一开过去，就能直接感受到那种低音的震动。

sentences.en: I would roll down the window and just, like, dance in my seat.
sentences.zh: 我会摇下车窗，在座位上情不自禁地跳起舞来。

sentences.en: That's one of the first times I really remember hearing Dembo.
sentences.zh: 那是我记忆中第一次真正听到登博乐的场景之一。

sentences.en: I'm Isabella Herrera, and I write about music and culture.
sentences.zh: 我是伊莎贝拉·埃雷拉，我撰写音乐与文化方面的文章。

sentences.en: Growing up in Chicago, I didn't really hear Dembo in the street anywhere.
sentences.zh: 在芝加哥长大的我，在街头其实并没有怎么听到过登博乐。

sentences.en: It was mostly something I listened to at home or with my brother.
sentences.zh: 这大多是我在家裡或和我弟弟一起听的音乐。

sentences.en: But when I moved to New York, it was everywhere.
sentences.zh: 但当我搬到纽约后，它无处不在。

sentences.en: And it was finally, like, someone gets it.
sentences.zh: 那感觉终于像是，总算有人懂了。

sentences.en: Like, I see myself here.
sentences.zh: 就像是，我在这里找到了自己。

sentences.en: I hear Dembo coming out of, like, a bodega or coming out of people's cars, just, like, blasting on the street out of people's windows.
sentences.zh: 我听到登博乐从小卖部里传出来，或者从人们的车里传出来，就那样从人们的窗户里在街上轰鸣作响。

sentences.en: Your body will uncontrollably move.
sentences.zh: 你的身体会不由自主地舞动起来。

sentences.en: I mean, it's definitely, like, the danceable.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它绝对是那种极具舞蹈感的音乐。

sentences.en: Like, you just can't.
sentences.zh: 就像是，你根本停不下来。

sentences.en: You have to bop to it as soon as you hear it.
sentences.zh: 只要一听到它，你就必须跟着节奏摇摆。

sentences.en: So Dembo is all about having a good time.
sentences.zh: 所以登博乐的核心就是玩得开心。

sentences.en: You know, a lot of the songs are about dancing or partying or doing drugs.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，很多歌词都是关于跳舞、派对或是吸毒的。

sentences.en: And because this is a sound that comes from working-class black neighborhoods outside of Santo Domingo, a lot of people look down on it.
sentences.zh: 正因为这种曲风源自圣多明各郊区的工人阶级黑人社区，许多人便对此看低一眼。

sentences.en: The Dominican government censors songs that they think are explicit.
sentences.zh: 多米尼加政府会对他们认为带有露骨内容的歌曲进行审查。

sentences.en: You know, people who are socially conservative really dismiss the genre as vulgar and obscene.
sentences.zh: 你知道，思想保守的人往往会把这种流派贬低为粗俗和淫秽。

sentences.en: Dembo is not the first genre that experiences that kind of backlash.
sentences.zh: 登博乐并不是第一个遭遇这种强烈反弹的音乐流派。

sentences.en: I mean, any genre that comes from the street often gets that type of criticism.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，任何源自街头的流派经常都会受到这种批评。

sentences.en: So, you know, if you dismiss Dembo, you're really missing out on a larger and richer, deep cultural history.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你对登博乐嗤之以鼻，你其实是错失了一段更广阔、更丰富的深厚文化历史。

sentences.en: It holds, you know, the history of Jamaican dance hall in it.
sentences.zh: 它蕴含着牙买加舞厅舞曲（dancehall）的历史。

sentences.en: It holds elements of proto-reggaeton from Federico, hip-hop from New York.
sentences.zh: 它包含来自费德里科的原雷鬼（proto-reggaeton）元素，以及来自纽约的嘻哈元素。

sentences.en: But Dembo's signature sort of style is that they crank the tempo up sometimes to, like, 140 beats per minute.
sentences.zh: 但登博乐的标志性风格在于，他们有时会将节奏飙升到每分钟140拍左右。

sentences.en: And it is, like, breakneck rapping over it, a lot of repetition in the chorus.
sentences.zh: 而且伴随着风驰电掣般的说唱，副歌部分有大量的重复。

sentences.en: And that repetition is super central to the genre and its catchiness.
sentences.zh: 这种重复对该流派极其核心，也是它如此洗脑的关键所在。

sentences.en: If you're just getting into Dembo, I think you absolutely need to listen to El Alfa.
sentences.zh: 如果你刚开始接触登博乐，我认为你绝对需要听听El Alfa的歌。

sentences.en: He is the king of the genre.
sentences.zh: 他是这个流派之王。

sentences.en: He is the funniest one.
sentences.zh: 他是最搞笑的那一个。

sentences.en: He is the wittiest one.
sentences.zh: 他是最机智的那一个。

sentences.en: And he is definitely your entry point to get into Dembo.
sentences.zh: 他绝对是你入门登博乐的最佳切入点。

sentences.en: You can really hear how hard he goes in Demagage Gigogu, which is his song with Bad Bunny from 2016.
sentences.zh: 你绝对能在《Demagage Gigogu》这首歌里感受到他有多炸裂，这是他2016年与Bad Bunny合作的单曲。

sentences.en: The title is a reference to the word Demagogo.
sentences.zh: 歌名是对“Demagogo”这个词的致敬。

sentences.en: And Demagogo is Dominican slang for someone who's a hater, someone who's a jealous person.
sentences.zh: 在多米尼加俚语中，“Demagogo”指的是那种满腹嫉妒、见不得别人好的人。

sentences.en: And the title is this, you know, really witty wordplay in the sense that it's, like, expanding all the syllables of Demagogo.
sentences.zh: 这个歌名其实是一种非常巧妙的谐音双关，它把“Demagogo”所有的音节都展开了。

sentences.en: It's not just a Demagogo, it's a Demagage Gigogu.
sentences.zh: 这不只是一个Demagogo，这是一个Demagage Gigogu。

sentences.en: That's how much of a hater this person is.
sentences.zh: 这人嫉妒别人的程度就是这么深。

sentences.en: That's how much of a jealous person they are.
sentences.zh: 这人眼红别人的程度就是这么夸张。

sentences.en: It's sort of like you encompass all of the possible syllables and vowels of the word.
sentences.zh: 这就好比你把这个词所有可能的音节和元音都囊括进去了。

sentences.en: I got to see El Alfa and to see the king of Dembo, someone who really came, you know,
sentences.zh: 我有幸见到了El Alfa，见到了登博乐之王——一个真正从街头走出来、

sentences.en: from the street and brought this music that has been dismissed for so long to sell out Madison Square Garden was huge.
sentences.zh: 把这种长期以来备受鄙视的音乐带到麦迪逊广场花园并创下爆满纪录的人，这意义太重大了。

sentences.en: I mean, you could hear, like, the chair shake.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你能听到椅子都在震动。

sentences.en: You could just hear everyone screaming the lyrics.
sentences.zh: 你能听到每个人都在放声嘶吼着歌词。

sentences.en: You know, there were Dominican flags waving everywhere.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，到处都是多米尼加国旗在挥舞。

sentences.en: I mean, it was really, like, a carnival.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那真的就像是一场狂欢节。

sentences.en: Like, it was so fun.
sentences.zh: 真的太好玩了。

sentences.en: It was constant movement on the stage.
sentences.zh: 舞台上的表演一直在持续变换。

sentences.en: It was a great time.
sentences.zh: 那是一段极其美好的时光。

sentences.en: He made a lot of comments through the show and, like, in his audience banter being, like, who said the Dominican Republic couldn't go global?
sentences.zh: 他在演出期间以及与观众互动时发表了许多言论，比如：谁说多米尼加共和国不能走向世界？

sentences.en: Who said Dembo wouldn't make it?
sentences.zh: 谁说登博乐不会成功？

sentences.en: As this kind of, like, celebratory moment for the movement.
sentences.zh: 这就像是为这场社会运动举行的一场庆祝时刻。

sentences.en: You know, my reaction was just, like, yes, finally, Dembo made it.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我的反应就是：太棒了，登博乐终于成功了。

sentences.en: I listen to Dembo pretty much every day, whether it's on my running playlist or my cooking playlist or, you know, just to get pumped up for something.
sentences.zh: 我几乎每天都会听登博乐，无论是在我的跑步歌单、做饭歌单里，还是单纯为了在某些事情前振奋精神。

sentences.en: And I think you should do.
sentences.zh: 我想你也应该这么做。

sentences.en: Okay, next up,
sentences.zh: 好了，接下来，

sentences.en: we're talking about food with my friend and colleague who has done a little pantry spelunking and has come up with a bottle you probably already have on your shelf and which I cannot spell nor pronounce.
sentences.zh: 我们要和我的朋友兼同事聊聊食物，她对家里的食品储藏室进行了一番“寻宝探险”，找出了一个可能早已躺在你的架子上、而我既不会拼写也不会念名字的瓶子。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Melissa Clark.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是梅丽莎·克拉克。

sentences.en: I'm a food reporter at the New York Times, and I'm standing in my kitchen next to the pantry.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的美食记者，现在正站在厨房紧邻储藏室的地方。

sentences.en: In this series, we're going to take a deep dive into the pantry.
sentences.zh: 在这个系列中，我们将深入探索食品储藏室。

sentences.en: God, you know, did you know I have two jars of marmite?
sentences.zh: 天哪，你知道吗，我居然有两罐马麦酱（Marmite）？

sentences.en: Why do I have two jars of marmite?
sentences.zh: 我为什么会有两罐马麦酱？

sentences.en: I mean, when was the last time you actually explored everything in your pantry?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你有多久没有真正翻找过你储藏室里的所有东西了？

sentences.en: What is this thing all the way in the back?
sentences.zh: 藏在最里面的这个东西到底是什么？

sentences.en: If you're like me, you buy a condiment, maybe you'll use it once, put it in the back of your pantry, and completely forget it's even there.
sentences.zh: 如果你跟我一样，买了一种调味品，可能用了一次，就把它塞到储藏室的最深处，然后彻底忘掉了它的存在。

sentences.en: Oh, sweetened black vinegar.
sentences.zh: 哦，甜黑醋。

sentences.en: I'll bet you have an entire meal in there just waiting for you to discover it and make it for dinner tonight.
sentences.zh: 我敢打赌，里面藏着一整顿饭，正等着你去发现它并为今晚的晚餐做好它。

sentences.en: I'm opening it up and, ooh, it smells so savory.
sentences.zh: 我把它打开了，哦，闻起来真香浓啊。

sentences.en: Well, I'm going to help you figure out what to do with all of those condiments in the back of your pantry, how to use each and every one of them to its absolute beSt.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我来帮你弄清楚怎么处理储藏室角落里的那些调味品，如何把它们每一个的美味发挥到极致。

sentences.en: Oh, God, it's so good.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪，太好吃了。

sentences.en: I love it.
sentences.zh: 我太爱了。

sentences.en: And today, we're going to talk about something that's a real pantry staple.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们要聊一种绝对是储藏室必备的经典食材。

sentences.en: Worcestershire sauce.
sentences.zh: 伍斯特酱油（Worcestershire sauce）。

sentences.en: Worcestershire sauce is absolutely essential in Caesar salads.
sentences.zh: 伍斯特酱油是凯撒沙拉中绝对不可或缺的。

sentences.en: You need it for your Bloody Mary.
sentences.zh: 你做血玛丽鸡尾酒也少不了它。

sentences.en: But what else can it do?
sentences.zh: 但它还能用来做什么呢？

sentences.en: And what even is it?
sentences.zh: 而且这东西到底是个啥？

sentences.en: So, Worcestershire sauce was developed in the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 所以，伍斯特酱油是在19世纪研发出来的。

sentences.en: It was actually developed by pharmacists, pharmacists named Lee and Perrins, in the town of, no surprise here, Worcester in England.
sentences.zh: 它其实是由两位药剂师——名叫李（Lee）和佩林（Perrins）的药剂师——在英国一个毫不意外的小镇伍斯特（Worcester）研发的。

sentences.en: Worcestershire is made up of four main ingredients.
sentences.zh: 伍斯特酱油由四大主要成分组成。

sentences.en: So, you've got anchovies, which have a saltiness.
sentences.zh: 首先是凤尾鱼，它带来了咸味。

sentences.en: They have an umami depth and a little bit of a saline fishy flavor.
sentences.zh: 它们带来了鲜味的深度以及一点点海水般的鱼腥风味。

sentences.en: You have molasses, which adds sweetness.
sentences.zh: 你有糖蜜，它增加了甜味。

sentences.en: You have tamarind, which gives a very bright, fruity flavor, almost like a citrus flavor.
sentences.zh: 你有罗望子（酸角），它提供了非常明亮、果香的风味，几乎带有一点柑橘类的气息。

sentences.en: And then you have barley malt vinegar, which is sharp and acidic.
sentences.zh: 然后你还有大麦麦芽醋，它口感强烈且具有酸度。

sentences.en: And all of those were fermented together with some other seasonings.
sentences.zh: 所有这些成分与一些其他调味料一起发酵。

sentences.en: There was garlic and shallots.
sentences.zh: 里面有大蒜和小红葱。

sentences.en: There were spices.
sentences.zh: 还有各种香料。

sentences.en: And when you ferment all of these things, they blend into this just very rich, very fragrant sauce with a bold flavor.
sentences.zh: 当你把所有这些东西发酵在一起时，它们就会融合成一种风味浓郁、香气扑鼻且味道醇厚的酱汁。

sentences.en: And it keeps for a long time, too.
sentences.zh: 而且它的保质期也很长。

sentences.en: So, that bottle of Worcestershire in your pantry, you can still use it, even if you can't remember when you bought it.
sentences.zh: 所以，你储藏室里那瓶伍斯特酱油，哪怕你记不清是什么时候买的，现在依然可以使用。

sentences.en: So, if you're thinking, well, where would I want to use Worcestershire?
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你在想，嗯，我到底能在哪里用伍斯特酱油呢？

sentences.en: Think about where you'd want to use Asian fish sauce.
sentences.zh: 想想你在哪里会想用亚洲鱼露。

sentences.en: Asian fish sauce has a ton of umami.
sentences.zh: 亚洲鱼露含有大量的鲜味。

sentences.en: You can just add a little bit to anything, and it's going to brighten the flavors.
sentences.zh: 你只需要在任何东西里加一点点，就能让整体风味瞬间提亮。

sentences.en: It's got salt.
sentences.zh: 它有咸味。

sentences.en: It's got that depth, that almost caramelized nuance.
sentences.zh: 它有那种厚度，那种近乎焦糖化的微妙风味。

sentences.en: Worcestershire sauce accomplishes a lot of the same things.
sentences.zh: 伍斯特酱油也能达到很多相似的效果。

sentences.en: But it also has a little bit of sweetness, and it has more acidity.
sentences.zh: 但它还带有一点甜味，并且酸度更高。

sentences.en: Fish sauce is going to be a funkier flavor.
sentences.zh: 鱼露的风味会更加奇特冲鼻（funkier）。

sentences.en: Worcestershire sauce, it's like the whisper of an anchovy.
sentences.zh: 而伍斯特酱油，它就像是凤尾鱼的一声轻声呢喃。

sentences.en: It's like, hmm, here I am.
sentences.zh: 它好像在说：嗯，我来啦。

sentences.en: I'm adding this, you know, this depth of flavor, this salty, umami flavor.
sentences.zh: 我正在为这道菜增添这种鲜味层次，这种咸香与鲜美的风味。

sentences.en: And yes, there's anchovy, but you can't really taste it because it's integrated.
sentences.zh: 没错，里面确实有凤尾鱼，但你其实尝不出来，因为它已经完全融为一体了。

sentences.en: It's part of the sauce.
sentences.zh: 它是酱汁的一部分。

sentences.en: But it's there, and it's doing work for you.
sentences.zh: 但它就在那里，默默为你发挥着作用。

sentences.en: What else can we use Worcestershire sauce for?
sentences.zh: 我们还能用伍斯特酱油来做什么？

sentences.en: Have you ever made a pot of stew or soup, and you're just cooking, and you're not following a recipe, and you're tasting, and you're like, oh my god, this needs something.
sentences.zh: 你有没有过这样的经历：煮了一锅炖菜或汤，一边煮一边做，也没有按食谱来，尝了一口，然后觉得：天哪，这汤里好像还差了点什么。

sentences.en: And you know it needs salt, but it's not just salt.
sentences.zh: 你知道它需要盐，但又不仅仅是盐。

sentences.en: It needs something else.
sentences.zh: 它需要点别的什么东西。

sentences.en: So in those moments, that's where you are going to go into your pantry, and you're going to say, okay, condiments, who shall I choose to put into my soup pot?
sentences.zh: 所以在这种时刻，你就会走到储藏室前，心里想着：好吧，各种调味品，我该选哪一个放进我的汤锅里呢？

sentences.en: Because you need that extra.
sentences.zh: 因为你需要那种画龙点睛之笔。

sentences.en: And Worcestershire is my go-to.
sentences.zh: 而伍斯特酱油就是我的首选。

sentences.en: A little bit of Worcestershire just perks up your stew.
sentences.zh: 只要一点点伍斯特酱油，就能让你的炖菜瞬间焕发活力。

sentences.en: It's almost like adding bouillon to your soup.
sentences.zh: 这感觉就像是在汤里加了浓缩高汤块一样。

sentences.en: You know, instead of a bouillon cube, a couple of dashes of Worcestershire.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，与其放高汤块，不如倒上几滴伍斯特酱油。

sentences.en: It's adding life.
sentences.zh: 它在为食物注入生机。

sentences.en: It's adding flavor.
sentences.zh: 它在增加风味。

sentences.en: It's adding verve.
sentences.zh: 它在增添神韵。

sentences.en: So next time you've got your pot of whatever's simmering, and you don't know what to add, try the Worcestershire.
sentences.zh: 所以下次当你砂锅里咕嘟咕嘟炖着什么、却不知道该往里加点啥的时候，试试伍斯特酱油吧。

sentences.en: It is there for you.
sentences.zh: 它随时准备为你效劳。

sentences.en: You know what?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: I'm going to try that.
sentences.zh: 我待会儿就去试试。

sentences.en: But I have learned to never sleep on a Melissa Clark cooking tip.
sentences.zh: 但我已经学乖了：永远不要轻视梅丽莎·克拉克的烹饪小贴士。

sentences.en: And finally, to send you off into your day, a new series called How I Hold It Together from The Well Desk.
sentences.zh: 最后，为大家带来一档新栏目，希望能开启你美好的一天，它来自健康专栏（The Well Desk），名叫《我是如何撑过去的》（How I Hold It Together）。

sentences.en: They started this little project during the pandemic, and you might recall it was very hard to just get through the day.
sentences.zh: 他们在疫情期间发起了这个小项目，你可能还记得，当时仅仅是熬过每一天都是极其艰难的。

sentences.en: But the series worked.
sentences.zh: 但这个栏目确实成功了。

sentences.en: They got through those days and many more days and decided to just keep it going.
sentences.zh: 他们撑过了那些日子，又撑过了许多日子，决定就这样坚持下去。

sentences.en: So here's Deputy Editor Kate Lowenstein on how she holds it together.
sentences.zh: 所以，有请副主编凯特·洛文斯坦来谈谈她是如何支撑下去的。

sentences.en: I told my husband that I was doing a story called How I Hold It Together.
sentences.zh: 我告诉丈夫，我正在做一个名为《我是如何支撑下去的》的故事。

sentences.en: And of course, he said, how about the first line is, I don't, which is funny because it's true.
sentences.zh: 当然，他说，第一行是不是写“我撑不下去了”，这很有趣，因为这是真的。

sentences.en: We have two young children.
sentences.zh: 我们有两个幼儿。

sentences.en: Our apartment's always a mess.
sentences.zh: 我们的公寓总是乱七八糟。

sentences.en: Things are very chaotic in my life.
sentences.zh: 我的生活非常混乱。

sentences.en: But, you know, I have coping skills.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，我有应对的技巧。

sentences.en: And I've been a health editor for a long time.
sentences.zh: 而且我当健康编辑已经很久了。

sentences.en: So I have a little perspective on which of those coping skills might be useful for other people to hear.
sentences.zh: 所以对于哪些应对技巧可能对其他人有用，我有一些看法。

sentences.en: So here's how I kind of hold it together.
sentences.zh: 那么，这就是我如何勉强支撑下去的。

sentences.en: I feel like there are not a lot of good breakfast foods out there personally.
sentences.zh: 就我个人而言，我觉得市面上没有多少好吃的早餐。

sentences.en: That's my hot take.
sentences.zh: 这是我的辛辣观点。

sentences.en: And I have decided that I'm going to start eating non-breakfast foods for breakfast most of the time.
sentences.zh: 我决定以后大部分时间都要在早餐时吃非早餐食物。

sentences.en: And it has lots of advantages.
sentences.zh: 这有很多好处。

sentences.en: One, you can eat your leftovers from the night before, which is very fast and easy.
sentences.zh: 第一，你可以吃前一天晚上的剩饭，非常快且简单。

sentences.en: Sometimes standing and sometimes with the refrigerator door still open.
sentences.zh: 有时站着吃，有时冰箱门还开着。

sentences.en: Two, it keeps me satisfied for much longer than a bowl of cereal.
sentences.zh: 第二，它能让我比吃一碗麦片产生更久的饱腹感。

sentences.en: I think spaghetti makes a great breakfaSt.
sentences.zh: 我觉得意面是很棒的早餐。

sentences.en: Delicious, spicy fish and cabbage soup.
sentences.zh: 美味、香辣的鱼和卷心菜汤。

sentences.en: I ate this leftover fried calzone for breakfast the other day.
sentences.zh: 前几天我把剩下的油炸比萨卷当早餐吃了。

sentences.en: It was not good cold.
sentences.zh: 冷了不好吃。

sentences.en: It was pretty soggy.
sentences.zh: 相当软塌。

sentences.en: But it kept me full for a while.
sentences.zh: 但它确实让我饱了好一阵子。

sentences.en: So my hips and back often feel very tight and achy, especially after I've been sitting for a while.
sentences.zh: 所以我的臀部和背部经常感到非常紧绷和酸痛，尤其是在我坐了一会儿之后。

sentences.en: And there's a spot like right on the side of my hip that's just always kind of tight and tender.
sentences.zh: 有个地方就在我臀部侧面，总是又紧又痛。

sentences.en: So something I find really useful is lying down on the floor.
sentences.zh: 所以我发现真正有用的是躺在地板上。

sentences.en: Sometimes it's just lying down on the floor that feels good.
sentences.zh: 有时候光是躺在地板上感觉就很好。

sentences.en: But then also lying on a trigger point ball, which is a like four inch ball that's hard and smooth.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，还要躺在激痛点按摩球上，那是一个大约四英寸宽、坚硬光滑的球。

sentences.en: And I put the ball on a yoga mat.
sentences.zh: 我把球放在瑜伽垫上。

sentences.en: I get down on top of the ball, kind of on my side, so that the ball is right under my right hip.
sentences.zh: 我趴在球上，侧着身子，让球正好在我的右臀下方。

sentences.en: And at first it's really tight and tense and it hurts.
sentences.zh: 起初感觉非常紧绷，很痛。

sentences.en: But then I do a few deep breaths and I stay there a little longer and I feel the knot release.
sentences.zh: 但接着我做几次深呼吸，在上面多待一会儿，就能感觉到结块散开了。

sentences.en: It feels like a massage where someone's going really, really deep.
sentences.zh: 这感觉就像按摩师按得非常非常深。

sentences.en: And if I stay on it for long enough, the pain kind of goes away.
sentences.zh: 如果我在上面待够长时间，疼痛就会消退。

sentences.en: So when I am finding myself having really overwhelmingly negative thoughts, like sweeping thoughts, like, I never see my aging parents enough.
sentences.zh: 所以当我发现自己产生极其压倒性的负面想法时，比如一概而论的想法，像“我从来没有足够的时间陪伴日渐衰老的父母”。

sentences.en: And my kids eat no vegetables and I'm so late on every story I'm working on that these sort of like over generalizations about how poorly I'm doing in life.
sentences.zh: “我的孩子不吃蔬菜，我手头的所有稿子都严重拖延”，这种对自己生活中表现有多糟糕的过度概括。

sentences.en: I've recently become able to notice when I'm doing that and think to myself, you know, what's going on?
sentences.zh: 我最近能够注意到自己在这样做，并对自己说，你知道，怎么回事？

sentences.en: Are you especially tired today?
sentences.zh: 你今天是不是特别累？

sentences.en: And usually that is the case.
sentences.zh: 通常情况确实如此。

sentences.en: And on those days, I say, okay, today you're an unreliable narrator and you're not going to take yourself too seriously.
sentences.zh: 在那些日子里，我说，好吧，今天你是一个不可靠的叙述者，你不能太把自己当回事。

sentences.en: And these thoughts are, we're going to just sort of hang them up and reconsider them later because they're being heavily influenced by how tired you feel today.
sentences.zh: 这些想法，我们要先把它们挂起来，以后再重新考虑，因为它们受到了你今天有多累的严重影响。

sentences.en: Not trying to have a conversation with myself about why it's not true or, you know, certainly trying to stop the spiraling thoughts about how it is true and just being like,
sentences.zh: 我不是在试着跟自己对话，解释为什么那不是真的，或者，你知道，当然是在试图阻止那些关于它是如何真实的失控想法，只是觉得，

sentences.en: all right, these are the thoughts we're having today.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这就是我们今天产生的想法。

sentences.en: Let's move on.
sentences.zh: 我们继续前进吧。

sentences.en: So there was this day last September when my toddler dropped my phone on the playground and it completely broke.
sentences.zh: 去年9月有那么一天，我幼儿在游乐场把我的手机摔了，彻底坏了。

sentences.en: I could not use it at all and I really couldn't believe how sort of free and untethered that feeling was.
sentences.zh: 我完全无法使用它，我真的无法相信那种自由和无拘无束的感觉是怎样的。

sentences.en: So I took a tip from my friend Tom and bought a lockbox that has no overrides, which means you put it in,
sentences.zh: 所以我采纳了朋友汤姆的建议，买了一个没有覆盖功能的密码锁盒，这意味着你把它放进去，

sentences.en: you set the time that you want to leave your phone in there and then you cannot get it out, which is a little bit terrifying.
sentences.zh: 你设定想把手机留在里面的时间，然后你就拿不出来了，这有点吓人。

sentences.en: But it has allowed me to feel much more present.
sentences.zh: 但它让我感觉更加专注。

sentences.en: You don't have that feeling of needing to check something constantly and I can read a book or sit with my toddler who's doing something maybe not super engaging and doing it for 10 minutes even feels really good.
sentences.zh: 你不会有那种需要不断检查某些东西的感觉，我可以看书，或者陪着我的幼儿做一些可能不是超级吸引人的事情，哪怕只是做10分钟也感觉非常好。

sentences.en: I'm Kate Lowenstein and here's how I hold it together.
sentences.zh: 我是凯特·洛文斯坦，这就是我如何支撑下去的。

sentences.en: I lie on a trigger point ball.
sentences.zh: 我躺在激痛点按摩球上。

sentences.en: I grant myself unreliable narrator days.
sentences.zh: 我给自己放“不可靠叙述者”假。

sentences.en: I eat dinner for breakfaSt.
sentences.zh: 我把晚餐当早餐吃。

sentences.en: I put my phone in a lockbox.
sentences.zh: 我把手机锁在密码盒里。

sentences.en: My son definitely did take the lockbox and lock it for two and a half days.
sentences.zh: 我儿子确实把密码盒拿走，并把它锁了两天半。

sentences.en: My phone was not in it at the time, but it made me realize, you know, that it can go wrong.
sentences.zh: 当时我的手机没在里面，但这让我意识到，你知道，事情是会出岔子的。

sentences.en: Well, our Saturdays together have come to a close.
sentences.zh: 好了，我们在一起的周六时光已经接近尾声了。

sentences.en: I hope you'll go find more NYT Shorts on our new app, NYT Audio.
sentences.zh: 我希望你能去我们的新应用《纽约时报》音频寻找更多《纽约时报》短片。

sentences.en: It's available for free to all of our subscribers.
sentences.zh: 所有订户均可免费使用。

sentences.en: Download it at nytimes.com slash audio app.
sentences.zh: 请前往nytimes.com slash audio app下载。

sentences.en: This episode was produced by Tina Antolini, Elissa Dudley, Sarah Curtis, and Tracy Mumford.
sentences.zh: 本集由蒂娜·安托利尼、埃莉萨·达德利、萨拉·柯蒂斯和特雷西·芒福德制作。

sentences.en: Edited by Wendy Doerr and Lynn Levy.
sentences.zh: 温迪·多尔和林恩·列维剪辑。

sentences.en: Engineered by Rowan Nemistow, Corey Schreppel, Daniel Farrell, and Sophia Landman.
sentences.zh: 罗文·内米斯托、科里·施雷佩尔、丹尼尔·法雷尔和索菲亚·兰德曼担任音频工程。

sentences.en: Special thanks to Paula Schumann and Sam Dolnick.
sentences.zh: 特别感谢保拉·舒曼和萨姆·多尔尼克。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Severson.
sentences.zh: 我是金·塞弗森。

sentences.en: Thanks for spending these past few Saturdays with me.
sentences.zh: 感谢过去几个星期六有你陪伴我。

sentences.en: And download the app.
sentences.zh: 去下载这个应用吧。

sentences.en: You're going to like it.
sentences.zh: 你会喜欢的。

sentences.en: I'll see you when I see you.
sentences.zh: 我们回头见。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·荣森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一个全方位探讨设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you.
sentences.zh: 甚至在黑胶唱片时代我在夜店当DJ的时候，每晚你都要带着300件你最珍视的宝贝去上班。

sentences.en: And you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你把DJ台变成了一个充满50年历史精美老物件的活体快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 立即在您喜爱的播客平台上收听由爱彼呈现的《重构者》。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。
